_whyThisIsTheRightNextTest: TRACED 2026-08-13: BaselineCarrierAmbiguityResolver.resolve is called unconditionally from DiffAttitudeBuilder.finalize (:263) and returns immediately at :104 because parseCfg_ (:395) reads cfg.estimator.diffAtt.ambiguityResolution.enable, which masterConfig.m:433 declares false and NO ladder rung sets. Measured on feat027: baselineIntegerFixAttempted=false, integerClassification='notAttempted', attitudeArMode='rawL1Only', wideLaneNarrowLaneClassification='disabled', wideLaneNarrowLanePairCount=0. This is a properly declared default-off feature, NOT a defect -- the resolver was never asked to run.
_whatItShouldDo: Stage 70 added a per-baseline candidate search (RMS cost, ratio test) and Stage 76 extended it to a joint L1+L2 integer-pair strategy with a WIDE-LANE CONSISTENCY SCREEN, |N_WL_float - (N1-N2)| < 0.5 cycles (BaselineCarrierAmbiguityResolver.m:221-234). If the integers fix, the 15 differenced observables stop being absorbed by float ambiguities and become pure geometry constraining 3 attitude unknowns -- which is the degeneracy feat025/feat027 measured (15 observables against 15 float ambiguities, exactly determined, nothing left for attitude).
_theGatesAndWhereWEALREADYSTAND: Thresholds from masterConfig:436-438 are searchHalfWidth 5 cycles, minArcEpochs 60, rmsThreshold 0.10 cycles. feat027's coarse search already measured a best residual of 0.060672 cycles, BELOW the 0.10 RMS gate, so the RMS test should pass. The discriminating gate will be the ratio (default 2.0 here, distinct from the attitudeInit search's 1.20) and the wide-lane screen. Read ambiguityStatus per baseline: rejectedRms / rejectedRatio / rejectedFloatDistance / rejectedWideLane each name a DIFFERENT physical failure, and which one fires is the result.
_ifITREJECTSthatISTHEANSWER: A rejection is not a failed run. rejectedWideLane in particular would say the L1 and L2 integer pair is inconsistent with the float wide-lane, which is the case where a genuinely geometry-free Melbourne-Wubbena wide-lane fix would add something the current screen cannot: the screen builds N_WL_float from N_float_1 - N_float_2, i.e. from the SAME geometry-contaminated floats, whereas MW is geometry-free by construction and so cannot inherit the attitude degeneracy. MW is also immune to phase wind-up, which is identical in CYCLES on both frequencies and therefore cancels exactly in N1-N2 -- relevant because wind-up is absent from this simulation and is the systematic most likely to tilt a flat residual surface.
_windUpCaveat: Phase wind-up is not modelled. An integer fix is exactly the operation an unmodelled slow carrier-phase rotation corrupts, so a successful fix here is OPTIMISTIC relative to reality on the L1 side. The wide-lane is the exception (see above).
